desk.why: Implied is only 1.00x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs. A reason to buy is present (realised vol rising above implied) but buying on it has not paid on this desk's history.

facts: NIFTY moved +5.6% over the last 7 sessions and +0.7% on the day, to 25,299.
Gap -42 pts, then the session added +86 pts.
The day closed in the upper half (close - low 156, high - close 85).
ATM IV sits in its 80th percentile of the past year: option premium is rich - selling it pays more, but moves are expected to be bigger.

base.why: History says moves like this usually carry on (it reached 25,500 in 70.7% of past cases vs 63.5% normally), so the plan sells puts at 24,800, under the writers' floor at 25,000 and sells no call below 26,000. Note: the desk's volatility rule says stand aside today (Implied is only 1.00x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs. A reason to buy is present (realised vol rising above implied) but buying on it has not paid on this desk's history.). This plan overrides it only for the scenario branches; size down.
text: bull put spread: sell 24,800 PE, buy 24,600 PE (credit about 36 pts, Rs 2,334 per lot; max loss Rs 10,666)

scenarios.title: Drifts sideways between 25,000 and 25,500
watch: Two daily closes below 25,500 without a new high
Close - open (the body) small, either colour
scenarios.means: The move is pausing. Time decay is working for the seller.
scenarios.action: Hold. Add a bear call spread: sell 26,000 CE, buy 26,200 CE (credit about 23 pts, Rs 1,472 per lot; max loss Rs 11,528) to turn it into an iron condor.

scenarios.title: Reaches 25,500 and stalls
watch: High - close bigger than close - low (sellers took it back)
25,500 CE open interest still rising (call writers defending)
scenarios.means: Call writers are defending 25,500. A ceiling for now.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 1,110 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell an iron condor, sell 25,500 CE / buy 25,700 CE / sell 25,300 PE / buy 25,100 PE. Call writers are defending 25,500: sell calls at the wall and keep a put spread under the market, so both sides earn while it stalls.

scenarios.title: Breaks out above 25,500
watch: 25,500 CE open interest falling (writers buying back - short covering)
Close near the day's high again
scenarios.means: The ceiling gave way. Next magnets: 26,000 then 26,500.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 1,118 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: or buy a spread, buy 25,800 CE / sell 26,500 CE. Momentum version: a bull call spread toward 26,500. Costs premium; loses it if the breakout fails. If it spikes past 26,000 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.
scenarios.odds: Reached 26,000 in 26.4% and 26,500 in 12.1% of past cases (normal 22.5% / 8.1%).

scenarios.title: Pulls back to 25,000
watch: Holds: daily close above 25,000 and 25,000 PE open interest still rising
Breaks: daily close below 25,000 and 25,000 PE open interest falling
scenarios.means: A test of the put writers' floor. Shakeouts are normal after strong runs.
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep today's position, or add nothing (weekly). If it breaks: close today's position and switch to sell 25,000 CE / buy 25,200 CE (weekly). Exact strikes for every expiry are in the position matrix.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,000 at some point in 42.9% of past cases (normal 45.3%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.
